- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates or overshoots after sharp moves; apply downward bias or smooth transitions.
- After a price spike (forecast > 68.5), model frequently overcorrects with a sharp drop; cap forecast decline to avoid excessive overshoot.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; introduce early mean reversion bias toward prior 7-day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate near the end of the horizon; apply a 2–3% downward correction for final 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model often misreads sentiment as bullish; reduce forecast by 1–2% for 3–5 days ahead.
